Colin Allred

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 33, Dallas County, Texas · Open seat

Attorney; former U.S. Representative and former NFL linebacker

Colin Allred is a Dallas native, attorney and former NFL player who represented Texas' 32nd Congressional District from 2019 to 2025 and was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2024. In December 2025 he ended a 2026 U.S. Senate campaign and entered the race for the newly redrawn 33rd District. He defeated U.S. Rep. Julie Johnson in the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff and faces Republican Patrick Gillespie on November 3, 2026.

Where Allred stands

Cost of living / economy
Says he will focus on lowering costs for working families. His affordability agenda proposes repealing broad tariffs, with exceptions for national security, and banning price gouging on groceries and consumer goods.
Health care / prescription drugs
Proposes requiring Medicare and Medicaid to negotiate prices for all prescription drugs, and using march-in rights to make companies license generic versions of some expensive drugs developed with taxpayer funding.
Immigration
His campaign says he would abolish ICE and move its functions to other agencies, expand due-process protections and access to counsel, end indefinite detention, and support a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and TPS holders.
Energy / utility costs
His affordability agenda calls for restoring investments in low-cost renewable energy to reduce utility bills. Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act's climate investments while in Congress.
Family economic support
His agenda calls for a stronger Social Security, paid family and medical leave, an expanded Child Tax Credit, lower housing costs through tax credits and affordable-housing measures, and more affordable higher education.
Ethics / congressional stock trading
During the primary, his campaign criticized opponent Julie Johnson's stock trades, including sales of Palantir shares, and argued voters could not trust her to stand up to the Trump administration and ICE.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas' 32nd Congressional District, 2019–2025
  • Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate (Texas), 2024; lost to Ted Cruz
  • Candidate for U.S. Senate, 2025; withdrew in December 2025 to run for TX-33
  • Won the TX-33 Democratic primary runoff over U.S. Rep. Julie Johnson, May 26, 2026
  • Former official at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development during the Obama administration
  • Attorney
  • Former NFL linebacker, Tennessee Titans
  • J.D., University of California, Berkeley School of Law, 2014
  • B.A., Baylor University, 2005
  • Graduate of Hillcrest High School, Dallas
